figures.caption: Thirty-six source documents are two distinct modalities. Nineteen of20audio recordings have Bashar context; the one Ashtar-attributed creator episode is a singleton. This is not a balanced sample of mediums or civilizations. Token counts use the common analytical tokenizer, not acquisition receipt word definitions.

Cosine resemblance of20complete unverified ASR documents in a shared audio-only TF-IDF fit, ordered by the exploratory KMeans labels. Diagonal values are self-similarity. Short IDs join sources.json; resemblance is not semantic agreement, independent origin or a speaker comparison.

Two-component TruncatedSVD is fitted only to20audio-source TF-IDF rows. The16publisher texts are projected using that same vocabulary/IDF and SVD. Marker shape indicates modality; colors denote source context/claimed labels. Label callouts reduce overlap without changing point positions. Author, format, length and modality confounding prohibit civilization-level separation claims.

NMF is fit to the20audio document vectors. Three display topics were selected prospectively for readable exploration; candidates2–6and seed-matched stability remain available. Weights sum to1per document. Top-term labels describe model components, not validated themes or distinct belief systems.

Overlapping predeclared keyword-family rates per1000common tokens, averaged equally across source documents within each labeled context. Counts are dictionary matches, not validated semantic coding. Source-attributed labels and modality are visible; singleton rows have no group-level uncertainty estimate. Promotion/footers and ASR error remain possible contributors.

Undirected union of each audio document’s two nearest TF-IDF neighbors with cosine≥0.20. Nodes are publication documents, sized by analytical token count; circular positions are purely schematic. Edges encode lexical resemblance, not social relations or independently shared ET knowledge. Threshold sensitivity is exported.

Nodes are explicit claimed-civilization/star-system dictionary families and labels give documents with at least one match. Edge labels give documents mentioning both families once per pair; audio and publisher-text panels remain separate. Zero-hit families are omitted from the drawing and retained in the complete count table. Positions are schematic. Star-system/Orion mentions can concern astronomy or fiction; ASR variants are not fuzzy-corrected. Bashar and Ashtar entity names are recorded separately and are not silently mapped to a civilization.

NMF reconstruction decreases with model complexity and is not evidence that additional topics are substantively real. Topic stability is seed-matched term-vector cosine; KMeans selection exposes all candidate silhouettes. Neither stability nor a selected partition validates a medium or civilization ontology.

Segments are assigned by their midpoint to ten equal decoded-audio-time bins. Each bin’s keyword occurrences are divided by its own common-token denominator; curves are equal-document means. The Ashtar curve represents one recording, not an estimated population trajectory. Bins are dependent and not independent observations; source intro/outro/advertising remains unsegmented.

limits: Modality, author, publication date and source-format confounding
Source-claimed labels do not verify speakers or ET origins
Lexical similarity does not measure agreement, truth, independent transmission or shared physical origin
No human annotation accuracy, causal estimates, significance tests or population prevalence are claimed
